headlines.title: Can the PlayPlace Actually Save McDonald's?
headlines.summary: McDonald's was once the largest playground operator in the US. Now, it's bringing back the PlayPlace just as its stock sinks to a four-year low — but can it actually save the company?*How to scale your business without selling out:* https://clickhubspot.com/69xtBy 1991, roughly 3,000 US McDonald's had a playground, and the logic was simple: playgrounds bring kids, kids bring parents, parents bring money. But unreported injuries, regulator fines, and ball pit horror stories chipped away at the brand just as fast-casual rivals started eating into its sales. Then came a $6 billion plan to rebuild McDonald's around speed. It worked through the pandemic, until growth stalled anyway. We dug through financial reports, court documents, and swab studies to trace how the PlayPlace lost a bidding war for floor space, what McDonald's gave up in the process, and whether its new $8.5 billion "Next" remodel can win back the one thing optimization never measured: a reason to hang out.0:00 - The playground that made McDonald's McDonald's1:15 - Why PlayPlaces printed money3:00 - From hot slides to lawsuits5:21 - Five trade-offs that often kill high-growth brands5:52 - Urban legends and ball pit swabs7:45 - The 2013 slump9:22 - Experience of the Future10:37 - The pandemic drive-thru win12:04 - Flatlining sales and losing the 'third place'14:16 - McDonald's "Next" and the PlayPlace comebackGet the 5-minute newsletter keeping 2M+ innovators in the loop: https://thehustle.

headlines.title: What Is McDonald's (MCD) Signaling With Its Faster Dividend And New US Chief?

description: McDonald's Corporation owns, operates, and franchises restaurants under the McDonald's brand in the United States and internationally. It offers food and beverages, including hamburgers and cheeseburgers, various chicken sandwiches, fries, shakes, frozen desserts, sundaes, soft serve cones, cookies, pies, soft drinks, coffee, and other beverages; and full or limited breakfast, as well as sells various other products during limited-time promotions. The company owns and operates franchised restaurants under various structures, including conventional franchise, developmental license, or affiliate. McDonald's Corporation was founded in 1940 and is based in Chicago, Illinois.
